newsitem.title: UK: Showery 30 days seen in UK, water worries remain.
newsitem.headline: Showery 30 days seen in UK, water worries remain.

text.p: Britain will get rain over the next 30 days, according to the latest forecast.
But it will not be enough to solve water supply problems created by Britain's worst dry spell for 200 years, water industry sources said.
The Meteorological Office's latest 30-day forecast predicts showery spells of rain, especially in the south-east, "with a few bands of rain moving east across the UK during the first half of June."
"The rain will do little to ease the groundwater problem," a spokeswoman for the Environment Agency said. "It's just falling on hard ground."
But it would ease problems with river flow. "All the rainfall will do is fill the rivers," she said.
"It's going to take a lot of rain over a prolonged period," to solve problems in some areas, she said.
Britain's new Labour government said on Tuesday it will hold a summit on water resource problems on May 19 in London, where it will put forward plans for action to tackle drought problems.

"This government is determined to take decisive action to tackle the causes of the problems which the experience of the past few years and the current drought has highlighted," deputy prime minister John Prescott said in a statement.
The conference will be held at the Queen Elizabeth II centre in central London.
Prescott will make a speech to the conference, which will be chaired by environment minister Michael Meacher.
